scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: Hi, this is Campus 2 -- both of our floors are having
trouble at the same time: the people on 10.5.0.x and the people on 10.6.0.x
say they can't get to their gateway things (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254) since
some reload earlier. We don't really know what those boxes are, sorry. Could
someone check why both floors lost their gateways and put it right? Thanks so
much!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: Scope and component: The “gateway boxes” for both floors are the Layer‑3 SVI gateways hosted on device sshswitch: br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24) for VLAN 5 and br_v6 (10.6.0.254/24) for VLAN 6. Mechanism: End hosts in 10.5.0.x and 10.6.0.x ARP for their default gateway and send to sshswitch via the VLAN-tagged trunk on ms1_sw4 (eth0.5/eth0.6 on both sshswitch and switch4). Localization evidence: On sshswitch, br_v5 and br_v6 are UP with IPs 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254, and the trunk subinterfaces eth0.5/eth0.6 are bridged correctly. From pcs: pc1 (10.5.0.1) and pc2 (10.5.0.2) both ping 10.5.0.254 successfully; pc3 (10.6.0.3) and pc4 (10.6.0.4) both ping 10.6.0.254 successfully. ARP on hosts resolves the gateway MAC to 4e:44:66:e5:55:8e, which matches sshswitch’s bridge MAC. sshswitch can also ping these hosts. Root cause: No current fault is present; both gateway SVIs are up and reachable, so the earlier reported outage is not reproducible now. Corrective fix: None required at this time. If the issue reappears after reloads, ensure sshswitch’s network configuration persists (bond0, eth0.5/eth0.6, and bridges br_v5/br_v6 with 10.5.0.254/10.6.0.254) and that ms1_sw4 remains a VLAN trunk; consider enabling a startup check/monitor to verify the bridges and VLAN subinterfaces come up after reboots.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly reports br_v5 and br_v6 are UP with IPs and that hosts (pc1/pc2 and pc3/pc4) successfully ping the SVIs, confirming baseline reachability.
